text: I now give the floor to her excellency
Anita Anon, Minister of Foreign Affairs
of Canada.
Mr. President,
excellencies,
colleagues, and friends.
Bonjour.
I was born in Nova Scotia on Canada's
East Coast and grew up there, the
daughter of immigrants.
Nova Scotians all know the same thing.
The tide does not wait. You must move
with it. The tide has turned in the
global order as well. As Canadian
historian Margaret McMillan has
observed, we have arrived in a new age
of disorder.
We are facing a rupture, not a
transition.
Great powers are walking away from
global economic cooperation,
dismantling economic integration.
Great powers want the rest of us to
accept what we are offered. And too
often, state sovereignty, the
cornerstone of the UN charter, has been
treated with disdain.
We are facing serious challenges in the
global order. But at their core,
Canadians and billions of others around
the world want to live peaceful,
prosperous, and predictable lives. That
is why in the face of this rupture,
Canada's goal is to achieve greater
strategic autonomy.
Greater autonomy to make our own choices
and to determine our own sovereign
future.
We can no longer afford to be overly
reliant on any one partner. Instead, we
are diversifying our ties and building
stronger relationships with new and old
partners alike so that our people can
enjoy peace and prosperity.
We will prioritize decisive,
effective action by forging issuebased
coalitions of nations that share a sense
of urgency on common challenges. We
believe that these coalitions are the
most flexible, effective, and immediate
way to address emerging global
challenges. We are already forming these
coalitions with small states, middle
powers, and great powers alike. Through
the coalition of the willing, Canada is
working with over 30 allies and partners
to bolster Ukraine and defend against
further Russian aggression.
And in regional groupings like the
Arctic 7 and the Nordic Baltic 8, Canada
and our Arctic allies are cooperating to
keep our region stable and secure. To
this end, I welcome Secretary Rubio's
convening of the Arctic 7 earlier this
week.
At a time when we are forming new
coalitions,
we should also strengthen the
multilateral system. This is why Canada
and our partners throughout the entire
world
have started a new initiative entitled
partners for multilateralism.
This initiative seeks to support United
Nations reform and reform of other
institutions to make them more
representative, more effective, and more
trustworthy.
A policy of values-based realism.
Understanding the world as it is, we
will make the right choices for
Canadians while being guided by our
values. We will diversify our ties. We
will work with trusted partners to
strengthen our strategic capabilities,
especially in emerging technologies,
critical minerals, defense production,
and clean and conventional energy.
And we will lead other middle powers to
act collectively and decisively because
middle powers are playing a key role in
building the framework for the new
international order which is being
established as we speak.
In the economic realm, Canada is focused
on what we can control. building a
stronger economy, diversifying our
trade, and catalyzing a trillion dollars
of investment in Canada. Over the next 5
years, we are exploring new
opportunities with partners in the
Indo-Pacific, the Gulf region, and Latin
America. This includes building renewed
partnerships with large economies like
India and China.
We are strengthening ties between Canada
and Europe.
Alongside the European Union, we are
building an alliance for the future.
Thanks to our strategy for Africa, we
are boosting our trade links with our
African partners.
We are making concrete progress.
Canadian exports to markets outside of
North America have significantly
increased.
>> Last year, Canada has secured more than
20 new economic and defense
partnerships. And at the first ever
Canada Investment Summit earlier this
month, we secured nearly $500 billion
dollar in new financing commitments to
investment in Canada.
As an energy superpower, we are
providing energy supplies to many of our
partners around the world while
supporting the transition to a more
environmentally sustainable future.
Because in a rapidly changing world,
Canada is a reliable partner and we are
ready to work together.
We are also ready to work together on
enhancing international security.
Canada's stepping up and taking greater
responsibility for our own defense. We
are making the largest defense
investments in generations, allocating
over $80 billion in last year's federal
budget. We are now spending over 2% of
our GDP on defense and we are building
toward NATO's 5% pledge by 2035.
These investments are strengthening our
ability to protect Canada and to
contribute to peace and security around
the world.
Canada is an Arctic nation and the
Arctic is central to our identity, our
security and our future. The Arctic is a
region of growing competition and for
many Canadians it is simply home.
>> This is why we are investing in Arctic
security
in consultation with indigenous peoples.
Their participation
is a key element of our commitment to
reconciliation.
As we mark the 30th anniversary of the
Arctic Council,
we continue to strive for a region of
cooperation.
And to this end, Canada has opened a new
consulate in Nuke, Greenland. And we are
strengthening our ties with our Arctic
partners.
Canada welcomes the recent agreement
between Greenland, Denmark, and the
United States to strengthen security in
Greenland and the High North.
This agreement is yet another reminder
that North America and Europe are
stronger together, and as a founding
member of NATO, our commitment to the
Transatlantic Alliance is ironclad.
Alongside our NATO allies, Canada
remains resolute in our support for
Ukraine. We share Ukraine's commitment
to restoring a comprehensive, just, and
lasting peace, one based on respect for
Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial
integrity.
Canada is dedicated to advancing the
unconditional return of Ukrainian
children, unlawfully detained civilians,
and prisoners of war. Next week, I will
host
with Norway and Ukraine a conference on
this urgent issue in Toronto.
and Canada with Ukraine
will continue to work together to
support safe and secure navigation in
the Black Sea by strengthening Ukraine's
port infrastructure and disrupting and
deterring the illegal activities of
Russia's shadow fleet.
Canada is also a Pacific nation and we
are absolutely committed to a free, open
and inclusive Indo-Pacific region. We
have increased our naval presence in the
Indo-Pacific and are offering the dark
vessel detection program to our
partners. We will continue to implement
UN Security Council sanctions against
North Korea and by working with our
regional partners, we are cracking down
on transnational crime, including scam
centers.
Canada's position on Iran is
unequivocal.
Iran is the principal threat to peace
and security in its region. It must
never acquire a nuclear weapon. Its
threats to navigation rights in the
Strait of Hormuz are direct affront to
international law. We join our Gulf and
European partners in strongly condemning
Iran's attacks in the region.
And Canada is deploying every available
tool, including targeted sanctions that
I announced this week to confront the
Iranian regime's abhorrent behavior.
Here at the United Nations, Canada will
again lead the resolution in this very
room in the General Assembly on human
rights in Iran because we stand firmly
with the Iranian people against
repression and for human rights,
dignity, and aspirations for a better
life.
Nearer home, the people of Haiti deserve
stability,
security,
and the opportunity to build a better
future.
We commend the many countries who
proposed their assistance to the gang
suppression force, in particular the
United States. Even if the population in
Haiti is still facing significant
challenges, we're encouraged by the
measures taken by the government of
Haiti to prepare for the elections,
a sign of progress and hope.
Throughout the world,
Canada will remain a voice that can be
trusted to defend maritime security,
international law, and the responsible
development of artificial intelligence.
We will continue to speak out against
the unacceptable rise in hatred,
including anti-semitism
and Islamophobia, which are plagues that
our countries must fight together.
We were tragically reminded of the
scourge of anti-semitism again when a
gunman carried out an attack on a
synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, on the
holiest day of the Jewish calendar.
As Canada navigates this global rupture,
our response is grounded in our highest
principles.
Canada is an open, pluralistic society
with a public square full of robust
and civil debate. Our success is
underpinned by this civility,
by our democratic institutions and by
respect for our differences.
As Prime Minister Carney recently
observed, we are a steady partner when
predictability is at a premium.
Canada's candidacy for the Human Rights
Council for 2028 to 2030
bears witness to our values and to the
nations represented here. We would be
honored to be able to count on your
support.
The rule of law is one of the pillars of
our society in Canada and it guides our
action abroad.
Canada's commitment to human rights and
international law is strong. This
includes our support for those
institutions that defend these
principles
such as the International Criminal
Court. remains unequivocally committed
to the charter of the United Nations
which Canada helped to shape.
Article one sub two of the UN charter
underlines a foundational principle of
this institution, the self-determination
of peoples. And let us be clear,
self-determination is a right to which
both Israelis and Palestinians are
entitled.
Canada firmly believes that lasting
peace and security can be achieved only
through a negotiated two-state solution.
That means a Palestinian state living
alongside Israel in peace,
security,
and dignity.
Israel's right to exist is not up for
debate.
And the right of the Palestinian people
to self-determination
in a state of their own is also not up
for debate. The two-state solution
remains the guiding principle of our
Middle East policy
and our actions are calibrated to
support this outcome.
Alongside our partners, we will continue
to target those who lead, arm, and
finance Hamas and other terrorist
organizations who threaten the security
of Israel and the broader region. Hamas
must play no role in the governance of
Palestine.
Israel's settlements in the West Bank
are illegal under international law and
an obstacle to peace. That is why Canada
announced earlier this month that we
intend to restrict trade in goods with
illegal Israeli settlements.

humanitarian assistance to civilians in
need
in order to respond to the urgent
humanitarian crisis in Sudan. We
recently announced financing to the tune
of $120 million to help the affected
people from Lebanon to Haiti to Gaza and
elsewhere.
We are supporting efforts to reduce
poverty, to strengthen resilience,
to promote gender equality,
to defend the rights of LGBTQ
to I persons and create economic
opportunities.
The United Nations system plays a
essential role in this regard.
But the UN is not and must not be a
static organization.
While the UN is experiencing major
changes, we should ensure that it is
ready for the future. We would like to
thank Mr. Antonio Gutesh for his efforts
over the past decade.
We are very much looking forward to
cooperating with the new secretary
general, be that a man or a woman.
President,

distinguished colleagues,
>> looks very different today than it did
when I was growing up in rural Nova
Scotia.
The tide has turned.
We could spend our time wishing that it
had not.
But to indulge in nostalgia or to give
into despair would be to let our people
down. That's not an option. Instead,
Canada chooses to move with confidence
and strength.
Though some would build higher walls and
retreat from international engagement,
we believe that long-term partnerships
are the way to prosperity and security.
Though some are turning away from the
principles of the United Nations, we
remain committed to them. And though
some would rather ignore the rupture
that we see before our very eyes, we are
willing to see the world as it is.
Rather than yearn for days gone by, let
us together take this opportunity to do
right by our people and build together.
This is the path that Canada will take
and we invite you to join us in
partnership.
